documents.unit: Academic Affairs Division / Office of the Provost
documents.title: UL Lafayette Guidance on Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
documents.summary: University-wide guidance from the Provost's office that applies to coursework and leaves the AI rule to colleges, departments and faculty. It lists areas a course policy should cover (permitted uses, responsible use and citation, penalties) and offers three sample syllabus statements.
documents.stance_why: Document sets no university-wide stance: it says it "encourages academic colleges, departments, and individual faculty to develop specific policies" and that faculty "will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use of GAI". It offers three sample syllabus statements (prohibiting, mixed, encouraging), so it is delegates with those templates as tiers.

units.why: Scope sentence: "applies to student intellectual coursework products at the graduate and undergraduate levels" sets what the guidance covers, so it is a scope statement (P56), general phase, informs.
units.anchor: applies to student intellectual coursework products at the graduate and undergraduate levels

units.why: States the purpose, "to promote ethical engagement with AI across the University"; a framework-level purpose statement (P56).
units.anchor: promote ethical engagement with AI across the University

units.why: "encourages academic colleges, departments, and individual faculty to develop specific policies" hands rule-setting to units below the university, so P85 (units set own rules) fits; the faculty-level part is coded separately as P04.
units.anchor: encourages academic colleges, departments, and individual faculty to develop specific policies for their students

units.why: "Ethical engagement with GAI, including restrictions, guardrails, or complete integration" will vary by discipline and by "skills and learning outcomes they seek to impart"; ties AI decisions to learning outcomes (P83) rather than naming a type like P04.
units.anchor: depending on the skills and learning outcomes they seek to impart

units.why: "All faculty have academic freedom in their classrooms and will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use of GAI" places the decision with each instructor (P04); no university default is set.
units.anchor: will be the ones to determine what constitutes proper use of GAI in their classroom

units.why: "it is the students' responsibility to familiarize themselves with relevant expectations and policies" because classes differ; the rule is that students find out each course's rules (P78), not just ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: it is the students’ responsibility to familiarize themselves with relevant expectations and policies

units.why: Instructors should "Define the range of uses of AI and be explicit about what you allow in your class", i.e. state expectations explicitly in the course (P09).
units.anchor: be explicit about what you allow in your class

units.why: Example permitted use: "Use of GAI to brainstorm and conduct preliminary research for assignments"; brainstorming is P15.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to brainstorm and conduct preliminary research for assignments
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use to brainstorm and conduct preliminary research for assignments.
units.fit_note: Also names preliminary research, which P15 does not mention.

units.why: Example permitted use: "Use of GAI to summarize articles and other readings"; summaries as study aid fit P14.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to summarize articles and other readings
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use to summarize articles and other readings.

units.why: Example permitted use: "Use of GAI to analyze quantitative or qualitative data" matches P89.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to analyze quantitative or qualitative data
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use to analyze quantitative or qualitative data.

units.why: Example permitted use: "proof-reading, grammar assistance, or to adjust style and tone" is writing support (P91).
units.anchor: Use of GAI for proof-reading, grammar assistance, or to adjust style and tone
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use for proof-reading, grammar assistance, or to adjust style and tone.

units.why: Example permitted use: "develop graphics or foreign language translations"; nearest type is P18 (prose-side tools incl. translation) but graphics are not prose.
units.anchor: Use of GAI to develop graphics or foreign language translations
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use to develop graphics or foreign language translations.
units.fit_note: Covers translation (prose) but also graphics generation, which P18 does not capture.

units.why: Example permitted use: a "draft or outline of a work product that is critically edited and expanded upon by the student"; drafting/outlining support under a student-edit condition, closest to P91 (outlining, revising).
units.anchor: outline of a work product that is critically edited and expanded upon by the student
units.policy: Instructors may allow GAI use to produce a draft or outline of a work product that is critically edited and expanded upon by the student.
units.fit_note: AI produces the draft or outline itself, with the student then editing and expanding, which is more than editing one's own writing.

units.why: "students are responsible for accuracy, bias, and integrity of any use of GAI" makes students answerable for what they submit via AI (P29).
units.anchor: students are responsible for accuracy, bias, and integrity of any use of GAI
units.fit_note: Responsibility is for accuracy, bias and integrity of AI use, not ownership of the work as such.

units.why: Instructors should articulate AI limitations and students' "responsibility to fact-check AI for both accuracy and bias"; verifying AI output is P31.
units.anchor: responsibility to fact-check AI for both accuracy and bias in results

units.why: "For courses where students may use GAI, require citations where there is AI usage" is a disclosure-with-submission rule (P24); it is directed at instructors.
units.anchor: require citations where there is AI usage

units.why: Alternative documentation: "saving and uploading for instructor review transcripts of GAI interaction, or screenshots of GAI sessions" is P26.
units.anchor: saving and uploading for instructor review transcripts of GAI interaction

units.why: "encourage students to participate in trainings that teach proper AI usage" is AI-literacy training for students (P70).
units.anchor: encourage students to participate in trainings that teach proper AI usage

units.why: Penalties should be specific by AI type, "potentially differentiating between grammar/punctuation assistance GAI and other forms"; this separates routine grammar tools from other AI, nearest P100, though it is framed as a penalty-clarity instruction.
units.anchor: differentiating between grammar/punctuation assistance GAI and other forms of GAI
units.fit_note: P100 exempts routine features; here the text only suggests treating grammar assistance differently when applying penalties, without saying it is exempt.

units.why: "the use of GAI in that course constitutes academic misconduct" when unpermitted; classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36). It also covers scaffolding work, not only final products.
units.anchor: then the use of GAI in that course constitutes academic misconduct

units.why: "Indicate grade penalties (if applicable) clearly and specifically" asks instructors to state penalties in advance (P37), without naming any penalty.
units.anchor: Indicate grade penalties (if applicable) clearly and specifically

units.why: Resource link "Sample Assignments redesigned to incorporate GAI" points instructors to redesigned assignments (P35); title only, no rule detail.
units.anchor: Sample Assignments redesigned to incorporate GAI
units.fit_note: Only a link title; no specific redesign is described.

units.why: Sample prohibiting statement: "Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate material is strictly prohibited" bans AI-generated submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate material is strictly prohibited

units.why: In the same sample, "All work submitted for this course must be your own original production" is an ownership rule (P29).
units.anchor: All work submitted for this course must be your own original production

units.why: Sample says AI-generated submissions "will be considered a violation of the University's academic integrity policy", i.e. misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of the University’s academic integrity policy

units.why: "This includes AI-generated material that you have summarized or edited" extends the ban to AI output a student has revised; prohibits submitting such output (P19).
units.anchor: This includes AI-generated material that you have summarized or edited

units.why: "This excludes AI-supported tools providing spelling and grammar checks" exempts routine features from the ban (P100).
units.anchor: This excludes AI-supported tools providing spelling and grammar checks

units.why: Sample mixed statement: "you may use generative AI tools for brainstorming and research" allows brainstorming (P15) under a limit set in the next unit.
units.anchor: you may use generative AI tools for brainstorming and research
units.policy: Students may use generative AI tools for brainstorming and research.

units.why: The same sample says students "must develop and compose your final assignments independently", barring AI authorship of final work (P19).
units.anchor: must develop and compose your final assignments independently
units.policy: Students must develop and compose their final assignments independently.

units.why: "If you have questions or suggestions for potential exceptions, please email me" invites students to ask the instructor (P10).
units.anchor: If you have questions or suggestions for potential exceptions, please email me
units.fit_note: Also invites suggestions for exceptions, not only asking when unsure.

units.why: Sample encouraging statement: "Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate a first draft of an assignment is permitted, but you must review and revise" is a prose-drafting permission with a condition (P18).
units.anchor: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) to generate a first draft of an assignment is permitted
units.policy: AI may be used to generate a first draft of an assignment, but students must review and revise any AI-generated material before submission.
units.fit_note: Permission for AI-drafted text with a review-and-revise condition; P18 is about prose rules in general.

units.why: "you are required to be transparent about your use of AI-generated material by following citation and documentation guidelines" is a disclosure requirement (P24).
units.anchor: you are required to be transparent about your use of AI-generated material

units.why: "You are responsible for the content of any work submitted for this course" is a responsibility rule (P29).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the content of any work submitted for this course

units.why: Warns that AI generators "are prone to factual errors, incorrect or fabricated citations, and misinterpretations" so output must be checked (P31).
units.anchor: they are prone to factual errors, incorrect or fabricated citations

units.why: "the university is training the future workforce ... increasingly exposed to and engaging with Generative AI tools" gives workforce preparation as the reason to engage with AI (P44).
units.anchor: a workforce that is increasingly exposed to and engaging with Generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Says the workforce uses AI; does not say courses must teach AI use.

units.why: "AI can also deliver results that contain significant inaccuracies and conscious and unconscious biases" states AI output is unreliable (P31).
units.anchor: AI can also deliver results that contain significant inaccuracies and conscious and unconscious biases

units.why: GAI "can answer questions, formulate problems, serve as a brainstorming partner" and "fuel innovation": names benefits without a rule (P87).
units.anchor: serve as a brainstorming partner

units.why: "It is our responsibility to ensure that we engage with AI in a manner that safeguards academic integrity" grounds AI rules in integrity (P95).
units.anchor: engage with AI in a manner that safeguards academic integrity

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines
documents.summary: Short Graduate School page framing generative AI in research, teaching and communication around transparency, faculty involvement and ethical use. It names concerns such as authorial consent and intellectual property and links to other university guidance; it gives few concrete rules.
documents.stance_why: Document frames GAI use in scholarly work around "transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use" and says GAI should "support research rather than replacing" human scholars; it bans nothing and requires nothing specific, so AI is allowed with conditions (permit). Mostly framing plus links.

units.why: "committed to preparing the next generation of researchers with integrity and ethical awareness" and using the tools "responsibly" is a framework-level purpose statement (P56).
units.anchor: committed to preparing the next generation of researchers with integrity and ethical awareness

units.why: "it is essential to use these tools responsibly" as GAI enters "research, teaching, and communication"; general responsible-use principle (P56).
units.anchor: it is essential to use these tools responsibly
units.policy: GAI tools must be used responsibly as they become integrated into research, teaching, and communication.

units.why: "emphasizes transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use in scholarly work" sets the guidance's principles for scholarly (research) AI use (P62); transparency matches disclosure but no rule is stated.
units.anchor: emphasizes transparency, faculty involvement, and ethical use in scholarly work
units.fit_note: States principles for scholarly work but gives no concrete rule on theses or manuscripts.

units.why: Names concerns of "authorial consent, intellectual property, and academic integrity"; closest is P52 (IP) but it also lists consent and integrity.
units.anchor: authorial consent, intellectual property, and academic integrity
units.fit_note: Also names authorial consent and academic integrity, and no specific copyright rule is given.

units.why: "GAI supports research rather than replacing the critical insight and creativity of human scholars" says AI must not replace human thinking (P32).
units.anchor: GAI supports research rather than replacing the critical insight and creativity of human scholars

units.why: "paired with expertise and integrity": AI should be used ethically and effectively alongside human expertise; nearest P32.
units.anchor: paired with expertise and integrity
units.fit_note: Asks that AI be paired with expertise and integrity; does not say who decides.

notes: Distance Learning 'AI Tools & Use' page not found (louisiana.edu/distancelearning/technology saved only navigation). Office of Communications & Marketing AI guidelines exist but are not about teaching/learning. No College of Engineering or School of Computing and Informatics AI policy found.
